title: Winfree Oscillatory Neural Network
claim: Local oscillators with scattered phases self-organize into coherent collective states through synchronization dynamics, and the same mechanism solves diverse tasks.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, big arrow labeled 'Synchronize', task thumbnails below each torus
description: Two pale lavender 3D tori sit side by side, joined by a thick purple arrow labeled 'Synchronize'. The bold italic title 'Winfree Dynamics' is placed above the arrow. On the left torus, purple ring loops around the tube each carry an arrow, and the arrows point in scattered, disordered directions. On the right torus, the same rings carry arrows that mostly point the same way, which shows synchronized phases. Under each torus is a row of three framed thumbnails labeled Maze-hard, Image Recognition and Sudoku. On the left they show raw inputs: a black-and-white maze, a photo of two zebras, and a partly filled Sudoku grid. On the right they show outputs: the maze with a blue solution path, a blue and red saliency or segmentation map of the zebras, and the completed Sudoku with filled digits in blue. The eye goes first to the tori and the arrow.
caption: Illustration of the proposed WONN. The network evolves on the toroidal phase space (S1)d, where neurons are represented as phase oscillators. Through generalized Winfree synchronization dynamics, oscillators self-organize into structured collective states, enabling effective computation for both image recognition and reasoning tasks.
abstract: Oscillations and synchronization are widely believed to play a fundamental role in representation and computation. However, existing machine learning approaches based on synchronization dynamics have largely been confined to specialized settings such as object discovery, with limited evidence of scalability to standard vision benchmarks or logic reasoning tasks. We propose the Winfree Oscillatory Neural Network (WONN), a dynamical neural architecture based on generalized Winfree dynamics. WONN evolves representations on the torus $(S^1)^d$ through structured oscillatory interactions, combining phase-based inductive biases with flexible and hierarchical interaction mechanisms instantiated as either fixed trigonometric mappings or learnable neural networks. We evaluate WONN on image recognition and complex reasoning tasks, including CIFAR, ImageNet, Maze-hard, and Sudoku. Across these domains, WONN achieves competitive or superior performance with strong parameter efficiency. In particular, WONN is, to our knowledge, the first synchronization-based oscillatory architecture to scale competitively to ImageNet-1K. Furthermore, on Maze-hard, WONN achieves 80.1% accuracy using only 1% of the parameters of prior state-of-the-art models. These results suggest that structured oscillatory dynamics provide a scalable and parameter-efficient alternative to conventional neural architectures.
